work.title: Fast dynamical similarity analysis

work.title: Comparing noisy neural population dynamics using optimal transport distances
work.notes: Noise-aware temporal comparison using optimal transport; a comparator for observation/noise controls rather than evidence that geometrically similar trajectories implement the same computation. No independent reproduction performed.

work.title: Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation
work.notes: Direct predecessor for initialization/path independence and useful test-time computation. Independence from initialization for a fixed input must not be confused with ignoring the input. Model-, task-, and intervention-specific results are not universal recurrent reasoning guarantees.

candidates.review_depth: Primary PDF methods and evaluation figure inspected in preceding audit; metadata reconfirmed

work.title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
work.notes: Separates training-time trajectory effects from inference-time halting/readout selection. Compare stopping policies on identical frozen trajectories; an improvement after retraining does not identify which component caused the gain. No independent experimental replication.

candidates.review_depth: Primary full HTML, predictive comparisons and discussion; canonical metadata checked

work.title: Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models
work.notes: Separates common score motion from answer-changing motion. Retrospective completed-trajectory opportunities and prefix-only prediction are different outcomes; the proposed geometric predictor must face mean-centered and richer trained comparators. Answer preservation is not correctness.

candidates.review_depth: Primary full HTML including scheduling, replay/hardware setup and cache discussion

work.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
work.notes: Reviewed v2 dated 2026-09-25. Existing depth-aware batching, boundary-stage scheduling, and cache-policy baseline. H100/controlled-replay results do not certify small-device batch-one energy or latency; fewer loops need not yield proportional runtime savings.

candidates.review_depth: Primary full HTML and selective-model limitations

work.title: The Curious Case of In-Training Compression of State Space Models
work.notes: CompreSSM; reviewed revision 2026-02-24. Controllability/observability and Hankel-inspired state reduction during training. Linear-system guarantees do not automatically transfer to selective/nonlinear models. Projection diagnostics alone do not establish a smaller executable model.

candidates.review_depth: Author technical report and reference implementation; canonical arXiv metadata checked

work.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
work.venue: arXiv preprint v1 and author technical report
work.notes: Jacobian lens; author report https://www.transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html. ArXiv date/authors recorded here; report release is a separate surface. Sparse local J-space construction is not one universal low-rank linear plane. Functional workspace observations do not establish subjective experience; code is unmaintained reference code.

candidates.review_depth: Primary proceedings metadata and abstract

work.title: Functional Alignment Can Mislead: Examining Model Stitching
work.notes: Adversarial comparator for claims from successful model stitching. A useful stitched predictor does not by itself prove native representational equivalence or identical algorithms. Keep task utility, adapter capacity, and mechanistic explanation separate.

candidates.review_depth: Primary ICLR proceedings identity and abstract; author code pointer

work.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
work.notes: Metadata follows the four-author published proceedings; the earlier three-author arXiv record is a versioned variant, not a different paper. Behavior-changing interventions can exploit dormant pathways. Retain the methodological reply and success controls; not a claim that all activation patching is invalid.

candidates.review_depth: Primary metadata and abstract

work.title: A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s "Interpretability Illusion" Arguments
work.notes: Methodological reply on subspace intervention interpretation. Keep both sides of the patching dispute and test control design rather than treating either position as a universal theorem. No independent replication or adjudication recorded.

candidates.review_depth: Primary full HTML in preceding audit; indexed abstract identity checked

work.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM
work.notes: Message-content and intervention controls challenge interpreting aggregate gains as communication. Receiver-solvability, sender-specific necessary information, shuffled/irrelevant messages and matched-capacity controls are distinct tests. No universal rejection of latent communication or equivalence from nonsignificance.

candidates.review_depth: Primary full article

work.title: Information Processing Capacity of Dynamical Systems
work.notes: Input-history function reconstruction separates memory and nonlinear processing under explicit input/readout assumptions. Capacity is not subjective experience, nor does optimizing a Lyapunov exponent alone establish useful task computation.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher/PMC abstract and metadata

work.title: Cortical Areas Interact through a Communication Subspace
work.notes: Online publication date recorded; issue publication 2019-04-03. Biological cross-area predictive subspaces are a methodological analogy, not a learned translator between arbitrary language-model states or proof of causal semantic transfer.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher/author abstract and metadata

work.title: Cortical activity in the null space: permitting preparation without movement
work.notes: Immediate output-null activity may remain relevant to later computation. Biological result supplies a horizon-relative measurement caution, not proof of a language-model mechanism.

work.title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
work.notes: Foundational learned adaptive-computation/halting precedent. Metadata check: Primary submission history says 29 March 2016, not 28 March. Pin the reviewed v6 separately from the original publication date.

candidates.review_depth: Primary arXiv identity/abstract and author explanation

work.title: Universal Transformers
work.notes: Shared recurrent depth and adaptive computation in Transformers. Recurrence alone is not a new architecture claim; comparisons must account for training, task, capacity, and executed compute. Metadata check: Pin the reviewed ICLR 2019 revision instead of a moving arXiv URL; original submission date remains unchanged.

work.venue: 8th ICML Workshop on Automated Machine Learning (2021); arXiv preprint v2

work.title: Analyzing Populations of Neural Networks via Dynamical Model Embedding
work.notes: DYNAMO learns representations of network populations from dynamics/outputs. It is a method comparator with its own fitting costs and assumptions, not proof that latent geometry identifies a unique algorithm.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher abstract and method scope

work.title: Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control
work.venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 15(1), 142–161
work.notes: DMDc separates intrinsic dynamics and measured actuation/input in a fitted operator model. Input observability, sufficient excitation, data length, and approximation limits matter; do not identify a high-dimensional system from a handful of recurrent states by assumption.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher/author abstract and metadata

work.title: Characterizing Dynamics with Covariant Lyapunov Vectors
work.notes: Covariant direction estimation is distinct from QR orthonormal frames and finite-horizon singular vectors. Identifying a functional role for a direction requires an additional task-sensitive test; no new algorithmic result is adopted.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher/arXiv abstract

work.title: Dynamical Entropy Production in Spiking Neuron Networks in the Balanced State
work.notes: Existing full-spectrum calculation for a specific balanced spiking-network model. Event-driven dynamics, finite perturbations, and smooth surrogate training gradients must be distinguished; no controller efficiency or consciousness claim follows.

candidates.review_depth: Primary publisher/arXiv abstract and metadata

work.title: Saltation Matrices: The Essential Tool for Linearizing Hybrid Dynamical Systems
work.notes: Reference for event-time and reset-map variational derivatives. Smooth autodiff or surrogate spike gradients do not automatically equal the actual hybrid trajectory derivative; grazing/simultaneous-event assumptions require attention.

candidates.review_depth: Primary arXiv metadata and full HTML method/calibration discussion

work.title: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling
work.notes: CALM: local early-exit confidence with sequence-level calibration and missing-state handling. Its population/risk guarantee depends on the declared calibration assumptions and does not imply per-answer correctness or arbitrary distribution-shift robustness. Independent-layer exits are not automatically recurrent-loop implementations.

candidates.review_depth: Primary ACL proceedings metadata, abstract and method scope

work.title: FREE: Fast and Robust Early-Exiting Framework for Autoregressive Language Models with Synchronized Parallel Decoding
work.notes: Existing synchronized-decoding and early-exit comparator. Fewer layers, hidden-state copying, and actual latency are different outcomes; copying hidden states versus projected KV caches changes semantics and must be tested.

candidates.review_depth: Primary arXiv metadata and full HTML risk assumptions/methods

work.title: Fast yet Safe: Early-Exiting with Risk Control
work.notes: Risk-calibrated early exits; reviewed v2 dated 2024-11-04. IID calibration/test sampling and method-specific marginal-monotonicity assumptions must be checked. Learn-then-test and monotone-risk procedures differ. Average exits/FLOPs are not measured deployment energy, and relative agreement is not absolute correctness.

work.notes: Relates training-gradient behavior and Lyapunov dynamics when learning chaotic systems. Forcing stability can destroy desired chaotic target behavior. Reconstruction of chaotic data is not evidence that chaos improves language-model reasoning or that every gradient instability is a numerical bug.

work.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies
work.venue: arXiv preprint; title variant reviewed from author artifact
work.notes: Title follows the reviewed primary indexed record and author README. A later Slot-Selective Evidence Masking title variant was found on secondary mirrors; latest version-specific primary verification remains pending. Four cells share a frozen Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct backbone and learned adapters/continuous packets. Author release records a formal preregistered floor failure despite large relative gains; do not promote it as a full preregistered pass. Evidence masks may change both visibility and usable role information. Author source: https://github.com/tokenosopher/populus-evidence-partitioning. No general causal-visibility claim or independent replication.

work.title: What You Can't See Is Still What You Learn: A Preregistered Sixty-Society Confirmation That Evidence Masking Drives Compositional Generalization
work.notes: Same-author confirmation with sixty shared-backbone four-cell systems, varying masking, markers and filler. Authors report a preregistered behavioral pass, but usable-role attribution remains unresolved because globally visible systems failed the marker-following check. Finite success-conditioned packet interventions do not establish causal mediation. Narrow task-family confirmation, not independent replication or a guarantee for heterogeneous C2C.
